newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Can sees Q3 restructuring charge.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Can sees Q3 restructuring charge.

text.p: U.S. Can Corp said Wednesday it will take a third quarter after-tax charge of $30 million to $35 million, or $2.23 to $2.65 a share, to restructure and realign is businesses.

U.S. Can said the total after-tax cost of the actions is approximately $14 million to $16 million or $1.06 to $1.21 a share. It added that it expects annual after-tax cost savings of about $6 million or $0.45 a share.
U.S. Can said the realignment will include the discontinuation of its metal pail business and organizational changes to make operations more efficient.

U.S. Can said it will close its Racine, Wis., facility after S.C. Johnson, a major aerosol can customer and principal customer of the Racine plant, awarded all of its global aerosol business to a U.S. Can competitor. About $35 million in annual sales will be affected.
It also will close its Midwest Litho plant in Alsip, Ill., which is primarily a shearing and coating operation. Business will be reallocated to existing plants.
The Sparrows Point plant in Baltimore will be closed due to increased efficiencies in other plants and the addition of facilities bought recently from Alltrista Corp.

U.S. Can also will close its Brookfield, Ohio, plant. It said the addition of Alltrista's full-service metal handling capability and foreign exchange rates unfavorable to export trade make this limited steel service center unnecessary.
The company said it also expects to streamline its organizational structure as part of the cost-reduction program.
The four plant closures and organizational streamlining are expected to result in pretax charges of $35 million to $40 million, with an after-tax cost of $11 million to $13 million.
More than 300 employees will be affected by these actions, U.S. Can said.

U.S. Can said it will discontinue its steel pail business, citing continued inroads by plastic products. As a result, the company said it plans to sell its North Brunswick, N.J., facility. That will affect about $20 million in sales.
Closure of the North Brunswick facility, if a sale is not consummated, would result in an after-tax charge of about $9.4 million. The cost would be $3.3 million.
